title: Estimate lifetime risk of developing or dying from cancer using ltRISK
text: lifetime risk developing cancer fundamental measure cancer surveillance public health communication. provides intuitive estimate probability individual diagnosed cancer specified remaining lifetime, conditional alive cancer-free starting age. Related age-conditional risks also useful communicating cancer burden clinically meaningful age ranges, age 50 70 years. Estimating lifetime cancer risk population-based registry data always straightforward. Cancer incidence, cancer mortality, mortality causes, possibility multiple primary cancers affect interpretation final estimate. Several methods therefore proposed routine surveillance settings, including Wun method (Wun et al. 1998), DevCan method (Fay et al. 2003; Fay 2004), adjusted multiple primaries (AMP) method (Sasieni et al. 2011), traditional cumulative risk method. National Cancer Institute’s DevCan software widely used estimating lifetime probability developing dying cancer. However, open-source implementations allow users compare DevCan, AMP, Wun, cumulative risk approaches single workflow limited. ltRISK package provides lightweight reproducible R interface estimating lifetime age-conditional risks developing dying cancer using aggregated registry data.
